verdicts.quote: “Vonage APIs (Voice, Messages, Conversation, etc) use JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) for authentication.”
verdicts.reason: JWT is the standard, app-scoped method across core Vonage APIs; Messages may allow Basic but JWT is the recommended and primary multi-tenant flow.

verdicts.quote: “To work with our APIs, you will need to sign up for an account. This will give you an API key and secret that you can use to access our APIs.”
verdicts.reason: Developers can self-sign up for credentials; Vonage advertises free starter credit with no credit card required, indicating self-serve free access.

verdicts.quote: “APIs to build connected experiences across any channel.”
verdicts.reason: Documentation spans many areas (Messaging incl. SMS/WhatsApp/RCS/Email, Video, Voice, Identity Insights, Numbers, Reports, Audit, Fraud tools), indicating broad surface.

verdicts.quote: “The Vonage MCP Server enables AI agents and developer tools to discover, describe, and use Vonage capabilities via the Model Context Protocol.”
verdicts.reason: Vonage publishes and maintains MCP server docs on its official developer site, confirming an official MCP offering.

verdicts.quote: “The 10DLC on-boarding process involves several steps and requires manual reviews by Vonage and its partners… Please allow several days or even weeks…”
verdicts.reason: It is buildable now with self-serve credentials and docs, but production messaging can require reviews and lead time (e.g., 10DLC, managed channels like RCS), adding practical constraints.
